**Group departure:** 12–16 February 2027, 4 nights in Rio de Janeiro

## What Awaits You in Rio

Rio reveals its beauty especially well from above. The cable car takes you first to Urca Hill and then up Sugarloaf Mountain. Far below lies Guanabara Bay with its ships and inlets, while Copacabana, Ipanema, the ocean, granite mountains, and Corcovado with its Christ the Redeemer statue stretch into the distance.

In the historic center, you will see colonial buildings, the unusual architecture of the Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian, and the Selarón Steps, covered with thousands of colorful tiles. This is another side of Rio, away from the beaches and postcard panoramas.

Another important part of the program takes place in Tijuca Forest. An open train climbs through lush tropical vegetation to the summit of Corcovado. Vines, palms, and enormous ferns pass by the windows; occasionally, you may spot toucans, sloths, or small monkeys. At the top stands the 38-meter statue of Christ the Redeemer, one of the city's best-known symbols.

You can spend your free time by the ocean. Copacabana and Ipanema are ideal for long walks along the waterfront, and in the evening the city gradually fills with music and people preparing for Carnival.

The highlight of the trip is a night at the Sambadrome. Samba schools perform in the parade: thousands of dancers and musicians, along with enormous floats, make their way along the avenue. Lights, drums, costumes, and movement continue for hours.

The itinerary is designed so that Carnival is not your only memorable experience. Before and after the Sambadrome, there is time to see Rio from different heights, walk through the central neighborhoods, visit the tropical forest, and relax by the ocean. Over five days, the city keeps changing: green mountains and water in the morning; lively streets and viewpoints during the day; beaches and cafés in the evening; music and lights at night.
